text.p: Tension in Turkish markets apparently eased on Thursday after remarks by state minister Gunes Taner that steps were being prepared to cut inflation.
Bond yields, which went up by around eight percentage points to 120 percent on Wednesday, fell on Thursday despite a cash shortage by 3-3.5 percentage points to 115 percent.
The most active paper in the market were April 1, 1998, May 13, 1998 and June 10, 1998 which yielded 115.33, 115,13 and 114.73 percent, down 3.34, 3.31 and 3.44 percentage points.

The market was 63.7 trillion lira short and the central bank lent 21.9 trillion lira at 74 percent on overnight, 29.4 trillion lira at 73 percent via tom/next and 5.0 trillion lira at 74 percent via tom/week.
The average overnight money and repo rates remained almost unchanged at 73.87 and 79.86 percent compared to Wednesday's 73.76 and 79.54 percent respectively.
The Turkish lira fell to 157,530 per dollar from the previous day's 157,300 as the dollar gained against the mark.
Domestic demand for U.S. currency which had previously emerged faded on Thursday after the central bank's heavy intervention late on Wednesday, bankers said.

The gap between the central bank's key dollar rate and the banks' bids narrowed to around 0.1 percent from the previous 0.6 percent as the central bank increased its key rate to 157,700 lira from opening 156,650 in line with rising dollar/mark parity.
